exposure: Treatment for the prevention of mother-to-child transmission of HIV
Booking status (registered vs. non-registered for antenatal care)
cohort: The study included 4,691 singleton live-births delivered at Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH) in Lagos, Nigeria, after excluding multiple births, stillbirths, and deliveries outside 22-41 weeks gestation.
finding: Older maternal age (>=35 years), hypertension, rupture of membranes, and not being registered for antenatal care were significantly associated with increased odds of preterm birth, while treatment for prevention of mother-to-child transmission of HIV was associated with a decreased risk.
gest_age: Babies included ranged from 22 to 41 completed weeks gestation; preterm birth was defined as 22-36 weeks, with subcategories for early (22-31 weeks), moderate (32-34 weeks), and late (35-36 weeks) preterm birth, compared to term birth (37-41 weeks).
